question:
(band=mild_tachypneic)
A 44-year-old male presents with a six-month history of cough, difficulty breathing, fatigue, malaise,
and unintentional weight loss of approximately 11 lbs (4.99 kg). He denies chest pain, palpitations,
sneezing, or nasal congestion. He works in a pet store with a variety of animals and birds. On
examination, his temperature is 98.6ºF (37ºC), pulse is 68/min, blood pressure is 105/83 mm Hg, and
respirations are 22/min. Chest auscultation reveals inspiratory crackles in the upper and middle lung
fields bilaterally. General examination shows muscle wasting and clubbing without cyanosis.
High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest demonstrates bilateral upper and middle
zone changes, including centrilobular nodules, air trapping, and fibrosis. Pulmonary function tests
reveal a mixed obstructive and restrictive pattern with reduced diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide.
Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid analysis shows lymphocyte predominance with a CD4+:CD8+ ratio
>1.5. A lung biopsy is recommended for diagnostic confirmation. Which histological finding is most
likely to be observed in the biopsy sample? Answer Choices: (A) Foamy alveolar macrophages with
PAS-positive inclusions (B) Bronchocentric granulomas with fungal hyphae (C) Poorly formed
granulomas with scattered multinucleated giant cells (D) Subbasement membrane fibrosis (E)
Macrophages containing dusty brown pigment (F) Caseating granulomas (G) Non-caseating
granulomas with concentric fibrosis (H) Interstitial infiltrates with plasma cells and eosinophils (I)
Diffuse alveolar damage with hyaline membranes (J) Interstitial giant cells containing cholesterol clefts
 A. Foamy alveolar macrophages with PAS-positive inclusions
B. Subbasement membrane fibrosis
C. Poorly formed granulomas with scattered multinucleated giant cells
D. Interstitial giant cells containing cholesterol clefts
E. Diffuse alveolar damage with hyaline membranes
F. Macrophages containing dusty brown pigment
G. Interstitial infiltrates with plasma cells and eosinophils

H. Bronchocentric granulomas with fungal hyphae
I. Non-caseating granulomas with concentric fibrosis
J. Caseating granulomas
